code_label: Fraud losses are substantial and growing
text_span: The staggering cost of insurance fraud is estimated to exceed 40 billion dollars presently and is projected to rise to $28 billion by 2031
rationale: States the problem magnitude motivating the study.

code_label: ML improves fraud detection capability
text_span: ML techniques have emerged as indispensable tools in combating fraud due to their ability to analyze large volumes of data
rationale: Explains why machine learning is relevant to fraud detection.

code_label: Novel feature selection mechanism
text_span: This study introduces a novel feature selection mechanism that may be used with any combination of redundancy and importance measures
rationale: Identifies a stated methodological contribution.

code_label: Quantum and conventional algorithms compared on home insurance data
text_span: it demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach on precise home insurance datasets by using both conventional and quantum algorithms
rationale: Describes the comparative experimental setup.

code_label: QSVM evaluated against suspicious conduct and false alarms
text_span: The project aims to use QML algorithms to identify suspicious conduct and false alarms and assess their effectiveness compared to conventional machine learning techniques
rationale: States the study aim and comparison target.

code_label: Quantum systems suited to financial transaction complexity
text_span: The intrinsic capabilities of quantum systems to manipulate and simulate complicated interactions between variables are well-suited for the intricacies involved in financial transactions
rationale: Provides the paper's rationale for using quantum methods in finance.

code_label: QSVM improves feature space analysis
text_span: The QSVM improves the feature space analysis, increasing the accuracy of the combined quantum-classical technique for fraud detection
rationale: Claims an advantage of QSVM in the fraud-detection setting.

code_label: Quantum parallelism used for pattern recognition
text_span: QSVM leverages the inherent quantum parallelism to process and analyze financial data effectively
rationale: Describes the mechanism attributed to QSVM.

code_label: Feature selection combined with traditional methods
text_span: This study employs quantum feature selection methods with traditional feature selection techniques to evaluate the effectiveness of the quantum machine learning classifier
rationale: States the feature-selection strategy used in the study.

code_label: Hybrid ensembles assessed against pure methods
text_span: this study introduces the concept of hybrid quantum/classical machine learning ensembles and assesses their model performance in relation to purely classical and fully quantum methods
rationale: Describes another methodological comparison.

code_label: Fraud detection requires meticulous examination
text_span: The insurance industry has a challenging problem in detecting insurance fraud, which requires a meticulous examination of the available data
rationale: Frames the analytical challenge addressed by the paper.

code_label: Heuristic approaches identify fraud indicators
text_span: Fraud detection has depended on heuristic approaches, which include identifying particular fraud indicators and using them to establish patterns
rationale: Summarizes prior fraud-detection practice.

code_label: Advanced analytics improve pattern detection
text_span: Enhancing our comprehension of the data through advanced analytics and machine learning algorithms is essential for improving pattern detection and reducing instances of fraud within the insurance industry
rationale: States the expected benefit of analytics for fraud detection.

code_label: QSVM runtime claim from prior work
text_span: Rebentrost et al. (2014) presented a quantum SVM with O (log MN) runtime for training and classification
rationale: Captures a cited technical claim relevant to the paper's method context.

code_label: Quantum kernels can improve traditional methods
text_span: Huang et al. (2021) found that Quantum kernels can improve the performance of traditional machine-learning methods
rationale: Summarizes a literature finding supporting quantum kernels.

code_label: Dimensionality reduction reduces quantum resources
text_span: Studies use dimensionality reduction methods to minimize the quantum resources needed for computing
rationale: Notes a methodological trend in the literature.

code_label: Quantum methods effective for anomaly detection
text_span: The results demonstrated the approach's efficacy in capturing patterns for anomaly detection in network security
rationale: Reports a cited effectiveness claim from prior work.

code_label: Quantum kernels created by feature maps
text_span: The work used quantum kernels created by quantum feature maps
rationale: Describes a cited quantum feature construction approach.

code_label: QSVM outperformed previous models in finance fraud
text_span: the QSVM performed better than previous models, reaching F1 scores of 0.98 for fraudulent and non-fraudulent instances
rationale: Captures a key comparative result from the literature review.

code_label: Quantum LOF showed speedup for anomaly detection
text_span: showcasing its superiority in processing big datasets with exponential speedup on data point dimensions and polynomial speedup on data point numbers compared to classical methods
rationale: Summarizes a cited performance claim about quantum anomaly detection.

code_label: Mixed quantum-classical fraud detection improved accuracy
text_span: demonstrating enhanced accuracy through quantum feature selection techniques and a hybrid classical-quantum ensemble model that outperformed classical approaches
rationale: Captures a cited result supporting hybrid methods.

code_label: Experiment compared three industry methodologies
text_span: This study conducted an experiment to assess the efficacy of fraud detection. It analyzed three different industry methodologies using the same baseline data set
rationale: States the overall experimental design.

code_label: Rule-based model used as benchmark
text_span: The domain expert rule-based model with no machine learning is deployed in the real world and provides a benchmark for the accuracy of the results
rationale: Explains the baseline comparator.

code_label: Feature selection reduces input dimension
text_span: a typical scenario of such an approach is feature selection (FS), which reduces the input dimension by identifying only a subset of all available traits
rationale: Describes the role of feature selection in the workflow.

code_label: XGBoost and SVM used as classical comparators
text_span: Classical AI/ML techniques such as XGBoost are widely used in various ML applications
rationale: Identifies the classical machine-learning methods included.

code_label: QSVM described as novel classification technique
text_span: QSVM is a novel machine-learning technique that uses quantum computing to improve classification jobs
rationale: Defines the quantum classifier used in the study.

code_label: Binary fraud outcome
text_span: The outcome of the fraud detection is a binary classifier, and each transaction can only be marked as fraudulent or non-fraudulent
rationale: Specifies the prediction target and class structure.

code_label: Dataset contains actual claims and SAR filings
text_span: The data set describes actual claims payment transactions and its features, volume, and dimensionality
rationale: Describes the empirical data source.

code_label: Personally identifiable information scrubbed
text_span: The personally identifiable information is scrubbed from the dataset
rationale: Indicates a data-handling constraint and privacy-related caveat.

code_label: Fifteen weighted parameters identified
text_span: fifteen parameters with weighted scores are identified to determine whether the transaction is fraudulent
rationale: States the feature-engineering basis for classification.

code_label: Engineered features provide discriminative value
text_span: These engineered features derived from the dataset encapsulate valuable information for classification tasks
rationale: Claims usefulness of the engineered features.

code_label: Heatmap used to inspect correlations
text_span: Fig. 1 depicts a heatmap illustrating the correlations between all features within the dataset
rationale: Describes the exploratory analysis visualization.

code_label: Feature map selection depends on dataset
text_span: Selecting the feature map is important and might differ based on the dataset we are attempting to categorize
rationale: States a design decision in the quantum workflow.

code_label: Quantum feature map defined as unitary transformation
text_span: A parametric quantum circuit may perform the unitary transformation Uφ (θ) on the Hilbert space ℋ of a quantum system consisting of n qubits
rationale: Defines the quantum feature-map construction.

code_label: ZZ Feature Map uses low-depth circuits
text_span: The ZZ Feature Map is difficult to reproduce using conventional methods and is executed using circuits with low depth on quantum devices that are nearly fully developed
rationale: Describes the chosen quantum feature map and its implementation constraint.

code_label: ZZMap enhances expressive power
text_span: By exploiting quantum entanglement and superposition the ZZMap enhances the expressive power of the feature map
rationale: States the expected representational benefit of the feature map.

code_label: QSVM kernel estimated on quantum computers
text_span: QSVM offers an innovative approach by leveraging quantum computers to directly estimate the kernel in the feature space
rationale: Describes the core quantum kernel method.

code_label: Quantum resources do not scale exponentially
text_span: the required computational resources do not exhibit exponential scaling with problem size, as observed in classical methods
rationale: States a claimed computational advantage.

code_label: Training and test phases separated
text_span: During the Training Phase, the kernel is calculated, and support vectors are identified
rationale: Summarizes the training procedure.

code_label: Accuracy comparison across models
text_span: KNN 97.3% SVM 99.0% QSVM 98.3%
rationale: Captures the reported comparative performance values.

code_label: Classical SVM slightly outperformed QSVM
text_span: The classical models KNN and SVM exhibit high accuracies of 97.3% and 99.0%, respectively
rationale: Reports the main comparative outcome.

code_label: QSVM promising despite marginally lower accuracy
text_span: Despite this marginally lower accuracy, the QSVM demonstrates promising performance
rationale: Preserves the authors' qualified interpretation of QSVM performance.

code_label: Predictions may diverge on specific data points
text_span: their predictions may diverge for specific data points
rationale: States a caveat about differing model outputs.

code_label: Results obtained through simulations
text_span: The results were obtained through simulations on a quantum computer
rationale: Indicates the study did not use actual hardware execution.

code_label: Future hardware implementation planned
text_span: Future works will expand to actual hardware implementations
rationale: States the planned next step for validation.
